title: feat(spec,lint): refuse a bare date-range preset name in an ordering filter comparand at publish time (#8793)
body:
Fixes #8793

The **C half** of #8690, per its maintainer ruling `5299879288` (delegated adjudication, 2026-08-15): refuse the declared relative-date preset vocabulary as a bare temporal comparand **at publish time**, in `packages/spec` + `@objectstack/lint`. The B half (engine door + analytics decline) shipped in PR #8808 and is untouched here; #8690 itself remains open for the PM to disposition. The empty-string cell stays its own card, by the same ruling.

## The defect

`last_7_days` / `last_30_days` / `last_90_days` — and their ten calendar siblings — are real, declared preset names (`DATE_RANGE_PRESETS`), but only for the dashboard date-filter positions, where the console lowers them to `{date-macro}` bounds before any query is sent. Authored as a bare filter comparand, nothing resolves them. Measured on #8690 (51 rows seeded / 38 in-window): `$gte "last_30_days"` → HTTP 200, count=0, silently; `$gte "{30_days_ago}"` → 38. Since #8808 the engine refuses the bare name on a declared temporal field at query time; this PR lands the authoring-time half, where an AI-generated dashboard is actually produced.

## Where the refusal lands, and why the split is shaped this way

The dispatch asked for the schema-vs-lint split to be decided by sibling precedent and stated here:

- **Schema door** (`data/filter.zod.ts`): a `superRefine` walk on `FilterConditionSchema` — the #7596 pattern ("removed as a check rather than as a type change") on the same file, and the #6227 pattern (`checkViewFilterRuleValueShape`) one package over. `FilterConditionSchema` is an open record, so the walk judges each node's own field entries; `$and` / `$or` / `$not` members re-enter the schema (correctly nested issue paths, verified), nested-relation subtrees are descended by the walk itself. This fires on every carrier: dashboard widget `filter`, dataset `filter`, report `runtimeFilter`, page/component `filter`, rollup `filter` — at `defineStack`, `os validate`, and the per-type Zod parse on `saveMetaItem`.
- **Lint rule** (`filter-preset-comparand`, new): the #3574 pattern — shared `filter-walk` traversal, rule-owned surface list (the same eight `validate-empty-combinators` declares). It additionally reaches the two shapes no `FilterConditionSchema` parse touches — view filter rules (`{ field, operator, value }`, alias spellings folded via `normalizeFilterOperator`) and filter-array triples (folded via `canonicalAstOperator`) — and runs at the **runtime publish gate** for `dashboard` / `view` / `object` / `page` / `flow` writes (it needs no resolution context, the same qualification `validateEmptyCombinators` records). Registered gating, CLI + runtime-publish.
- **Vocabulary re-homed** (`data/date-range-presets.ts`): `DATE_RANGE_PRESETS` moved from `ui/dashboard.zod.ts` to `data/` because the refusal in `data/filter.zod.ts` cannot import from `ui/` without a cycle (`ui/dashboard.zod.ts` already imports `data/filter.zod.ts`). The `ui` module re-exports it — both import paths keep working, one declaration (`check:dual-source-exports` clean). New exports: `isDateRangePresetName`, `DATE_RANGE_PRESET_MACRO_WINDOWS` (the per-preset macro window the refusals quote — pinned member-by-member against the real macro vocabulary so a prescription can never name a token the resolver rejects), and the shared message builder (one wording for the two moments, the #5240 convention).

**Refusal identity:** the ruling says reuse the settled pattern rather than mint one. Measured against the loud path one branch over: `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` is core's runtime token refusal and was deliberately NOT borrowed (the #8808 door records why: nothing here is a token). The publish-time siblings are zod `custom` issues with prescriptive messages (schema) and a `filter-*` rule id in the #3574 finding shape (lint) — both reused exactly.

## The boundary — ordering positions only, stated as the load-bearing decision

- **Judged:** `$gt` / `$gte` / `$lt` / `$lte` comparands, `$between` endpoints, ordering triples (`'>'`, `'>='`, `'gt'`, `'after'`, …), ordering view rules (`greater_than`, `before`, `after`, `between`, + aliases). An ordered comparison against a declared preset name has no legitimate reading anywhere.
- **Deliberately not judged:** equality and membership. A select/picklist column legitimately stores values colliding with preset names — `GlobalFilterSchema`'s own pins protect `type: 'select', defaultValue: 'this_quarter'` — and this layer is field-agnostic (the schema says so at #5685 length). On a declared temporal field the engine door already refuses equality with the field type in hand, loudly, at query time. Refusing it blind here would trade a silent zero for false rejections — the #6227 doctrine ("a publish-time gate refusing more than the query path refuses"), applied in the one place it bends: ordering-against-a-declared-vocabulary-word, which the ruling itself classifies as never-valid semantics.
- **Only the 13 declared names** — never a guessed superset (`last_60_days` stays the engine door's field-typed business). `{placeholder}` spellings never collide (a preset carries no braces), so this and `filter-token-unknown` cannot double-report one value. Empty string untouched.

## ADR-0087

Semantic entry `filter-preset-ordering-comparand-refused` registered under protocol major 18 — the `view-filter-rule-value-shaped-by-operator` precedent (a publish-time gate catching up to a query-time one; no D2 conversion, because the shape was never written by any first-party producer and never executed usefully). Changeset carries the marker; `check-adr-0087-registration` green.

## os-regen relay — this PR touches `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`

Sibling **PR #8932 (#8715) landed on `main` (`2c86fe3`)** adding the retired-def:18 region while this branch was open. The relay was run per `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh`: merge committed **first** (one hand-resolved conflict in `registry.ts` — both branches inserted a semantic:18 entry at the same sorted position; resolved as the stacked union), then the full regen chain (`gen:migration-registry`, spec build, `check:generated --fix` — `api-surface` + `export-origins` only, `gen:spec-changes`, `gen:upgrade-guide`, `gen:openapi` restore). Asserted surviving on the merged tree: this branch's `filter-preset-ordering-comparand-refused` entry (1 hit), #8932's `identity-api-key-schema-retired` entry (1 hit), **and** #8932's implementation body — `export const ApiKeySchema` remains absent from `packages/spec/src/`. `check:generated` reports all 13 artifacts up to date at the final head.

## Optional extension NOT taken — the declared `StrategyContext` hook

The inherited brief (issue comment `5300389639`) offered a declared classification hook on `StrategyContext` with a binding loud-absence constraint. Not taken, and C-alone is the sanctioned complete deliverable, because the two constraints cannot both be honoured from this card: the hook's consumer is `NativeSQLStrategy` (`service-analytics`), which this card's own 裁决 forbids touching — and a spec-only declaration nothing reads is declared-but-unenforced surface (PD #10 / ADR-0078), while "absence must be loud" requires exactly the consumer-side change that is out of bounds. The rejected identity-proxy mechanism was not re-proposed. The residual stays as #8808 shipped it (cube-dimension classification as the floor); a follow-up pairing `spec` + `service-analytics` in one dispatch is the shape that could take it up.

## Fixture triage (three dispositions, measured)

Grep of the full declared list across `packages/` and `examples/`: every hit is a comment, a B-half engine-level test (which pins the *engine's* refusal and does not parse through `FilterConditionSchema`), or a legitimate dashboard position (`defaultRange` / date-filter `defaultValue`) — the positions that stay accepted. **Zero fixtures re-spelled, zero replaced** — the shipped `system_overview` dashboard's `defaultValue: 'last_7_days'` keeps validating, pinned.

## Verification — union re-run after the final commit, at **`6354f45`**, clean tree

- `@objectstack/spec` — **405 files / 10,711 tests passed**; `typecheck` clean (incl. `check:test-typecheck`); `check:generated` — **all 13 artifacts up to date**.
- `@objectstack/lint` — **73 files / 2,045 tests passed**; `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`) clean. The runtime-gate/wiring enumeration pins that exist to make dispatch-widening deliberate were updated to name the new rule — that diff is this PR's declared intent, not collateral.
- **Ratchet family at `6354f45`**: `check:type-check-coverage` OK; `--re-measure` — **33 ledger entries, 1,926 raw errors, none above its recorded number**, on the **fully built workspace closure** (`turbo run build --filter=./packages/* --filter=./packages/*/*` first — an unbuilt tree makes this gate refuse outright). The one red CI caught at `f0a5202` (lint TEST_DEBT 20 → 22) was two errors downstream of one extensionless test import (TS2835 + two TS7006) — fixed at the source in `af7d667`, **ledger not raised**; lint's test layer now measures 19 vs recorded 20 (the 1-error surplus pre-dates this branch and is noted, not silently absorbed).
- Root gates at `6354f45`, all PASS: `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs` (pnpm + node), `check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:merge-driver`, `check:objectui-changeset`, `check:spec-parsed-alias`, `check:type-source-resolution`, `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-empty-changeset`, `check-dev-prereqs`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:query-options-erasure`.
- Consumer sweep (downstream direction — consumers of `@objectstack/spec`, run at the pre-merge tree `f0a5202`, my diff unchanged in those packages since): `@objectstack/core` **838 passed**; `@objectstack/objectql` **3,675 passed untouched** (B half stays green); example apps `app-showcase` / `app-crm` / `app-todo` `objectstack validate` all exit 0 (pre-existing advisories only).
- **Refusal pins + discriminating positive controls in the same files**: every declared preset × every ordering operator asserts the zod issue `code` + `path` + message shape (offending value, `{30_days_ago}` macro fix, ISO alternative, #8793); the same suites hold `{30_days_ago}`, ISO dates, `Date` objects, `$field` references, equality/membership preset collisions, undeclared strings, and the empty string **accepted**. The dashboard-embedding pin proves the refusal surfaces through `DashboardSchema.parse` with the full nested path.
- Gate list re-derived from the actual changed paths (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`): it added `check:objectui-changeset` / `check-changeset-no-major` / `check-empty-changeset` beyond the dispatch prompt's list; all run.
